summary: Los Angeles County's 1927 steel lookout on Mount Islip reportedly moved to South Mount Hawkins in 1938; the stone cabin and tower footings remain.

facts.design: 22-foot X-brace steel tower with an 8x8 observation cabin, and a stone residence cabin nearby
facts.status_note: The tower left the summit in 1938. The stone cabin ruin and concrete tower footings remain.

access.note: Reached on hiking trails in the Angeles National Forest.

visit.trail_note: Modern Hiker describes a 7-mile hike from Islip Saddle; the Forest Service lists a 0.85-mile Mt. Islip Trail from Windy Gap.

events.note: Steel tower and 8x8 cabin erected for the county; stone residence cabin nearby
A federal forest lookout was reported at the tower in August 1938
Tower reportedly moved to South Mount Hawkins
Register says a later structure stood until 2002; the register text does not place it

corrections.why: The register and Angeles Adventures both describe a 22-foot steel tower; neither gives 100 feet, and the 30.5 m figure has no source in what was read. Confirm against a photo or second source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register names the Los Angeles County Fire Department; Angeles Adventures and the 1927 newspaper accounts name the county forestry department. The story reports both.

The register and Angeles Adventures give 1927. Newspapers show work begun in September 1927, the tower in use by June 1928, and a January 1929 report describing its erection as work done during the year. The story keeps 1927 as the build date.
The register gives 8,262 ft; a 1927 announcement said 8,000 ft and a January 1929 report said 8,240 ft.

notes_for_editor: History rests on the register and Angeles Adventures, with newspaper transcripts for 1927-1938. The brief's 30.5 m height is not supported by anything read; the 22-foot tower figure is proposed as a correction, so check it. The register and Angeles Adventures disagree on the agency. The register text does not place the later 2002 structure, so the story does not say where it stood. The trailheads differ (Islip Saddle per Modern Hiker, Windy Gap per the Forest Service); both routes are public trails. The firelookout.org California index also has an 'Islip, Mount' row with FFLOS US 2083 and NHLR US 1057 marked Gone; I did not open it, so a possible duplicate record is unchecked.
